ledger.claim: The rider's own instruction in the chat log asked the driver to stop at IMM first, and the driver agreed. That is a rider-requested additional stop on its face, and it is the driver's best exculpatory hook under POL-RD-04. But the clause requires the gps_trace to corroborate the instruction: the vehicle must pass within 200 m of the waypoint named by chat_message.waypoint_hint. The platform's own derived waypoint_approach block shows the nearest fix to the IMM hint (1.3348, 103.7466) was 3088.34 m away, and within_threshold is false. The instruction therefore did not cause the measured excess, POL-RD-04 does not apply, no distance is excluded, and the deviation is decided on the trace as measured under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02.

The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 23.79 km, against an optimal_distance_km of 18.3 km stored on the trip record at booking. Excess is 5.49 km, which is 30.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute. The rider's claim that the trip was 23.79 km for 18.3 km is therefore correct on the trace figure, and the trip_record.actual_distance_km of 23.8 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test.

ruling.explanation:
Rider: your route-deviation complaint succeeds in part. Driver: you are not exonerated. The trip from Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres to Blk 130 Bukit Batok West Ave 6 is measured at 23.79 km on the GPS trace against a booked optimal route of 18.3 km — an excess of 5.49 km, or 30.0% of optimal (EV-GPS-02856, EV-TRIP-02856). Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests are met (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km absolute), so the deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The trace figure governs over the rounded 23.8 km trip-record copy. The excess is below both materiality gates (50% of optimal, or 8.0 km), so this is a deviation but not a MATERIAL one. | Driver, your answer is that the rider asked for IMM. That instruction is real: MSG-02856-001, sent by the rider at 15:33:19 — one minute after the meter started — and you replied 'ok' at 15:33:34. POL-RD-04 exonerates only where the trace corroborates the instruction, and POL-RD-14 governs where it does not. The platform's waypoint analysis puts the nearest fix to the IMM hint (1.3348, 103.7466) 3,088.34 m away, and within_threshold is false. The request was made and the route did not follow it, which is a failed corroboration, not the balanced contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes. No distance is excluded; the deviation stands on the trace as measured. Your counterparty statement — that the rider asked for IMM — is accepted so far as it goes, but it does not show the detour was actually driven, and the rider's own account is the opposite: you never went to IMM. | The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs arithmetically. Charged total: $31.13. Recomputed fare on the optimal route: (($3.80 + $0.75 x 18.3 km + $0.28 x 24.7 min) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + $0.80 platform fee + $0 ERP = $25.2410 (EV-FARE-02856). Refund = $31.13 - $25.2410 = $5.8890, rounded up to $5.90. That is above the $0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of $5.90. | No ERP, toll or surcharge correction is due under POL-RD-09: the fare breakdown carries zero gantries, zero tolls and no airport surcharge line, so there is nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and no phantom line to refund. No billing-integrity referral follows. | No traffic advisory was on file for this trip: EV-ADVIS-02856-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. No party cited an advisory identifier as an exculpatory record, so under POL-RD-13 the gap is a bundle gap, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable and no traffic cause reduces the excess or supplies an amended optimal. | The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 187 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires — identifiers and pickup timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the trace is clean; the refund is far below the $150 ceiling and below charged_total; and there are no unexplained charge lines. | The driver's profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 408 completed trips in 90 days), so POL-RD-06 neither uplifts the remedy nor makes a conduct referral; the excess is not MATERIAL in any event. The rider's profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration requirement (deviation_claims_60d 1). No driver compensation arises under POL-RD-04: the billed distance (23.8 km) is not more than 1.0 km short of the trace distance (23.79 km). | Confidence is 0.9, capped by the deciding artifacts, all at weight_multiplier 1.0; the only impaired artifact is the absent advisory, which carries no deciding fact. The monetary effect of $5.90 is at or below the $8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it executes on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
